subject: Mathematics
title: Complex Numbers and Quadratic Equations
summary: A complex number z = x + iy (i² = −1) is a point (x, y) in the Argand plane. Modulus |z| = distance from the origin; argument arg z = angle from the positive x-axis. The polar form z = r(cos θ + i sin θ) = re^{iθ} makes multiplication and powers easy.
The conjugate z̄ = x − iy is the reflection in the real axis. z z̄ = |z|², |z₁z₂| = |z₁||z₂|, arg(z₁z₂) = arg z₁ + arg z₂ — almost every JEE simplification uses these.
Cube roots of unity 1, ω, ω² (1 + ω + ω² = 0, ω³ = 1) are a separate favourite. Locus questions use |z − z₁| = r (circle) and |z − z₁| = |z − z₂| (perpendicular bisector).
The roots of ax² + bx + c = 0 are (−b ± √D)/2a; D = b² − 4ac decides their nature. Sum = −b/a, product = c/a — these give symmetric expressions and new equations without finding the roots.

formulas.name: Powers of i
formulas.formula: i² = −1, i³ = −i, i⁴ = 1;  iⁿ = i^{n mod 4};  i + i² + i³ + i⁴ = 0
formulas.mistake: √a √b = √(ab) only when both are non-negative; √(−4)√(−9) = −6, not +6.

formulas.name: Algebra of complex numbers
formulas.formula: (a + ib) ± (c + id) = (a ± c) + i(b ± d);  (a + ib)(c + id) = (ac − bd) + i(ad + bc);  division: multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the denominator

formulas.name: Conjugate properties
formulas.formula: z + z̄ = 2 Re z;  z − z̄ = 2i Im z;  z z̄ = |z|²;  conj(z₁ ± z₂) = z̄₁ ± z̄₂;  conj(z₁z₂) = z̄₁z̄₂;  z real ⇔ z = z̄;  purely imaginary ⇔ z = −z̄

formulas.name: Triangle inequality
formulas.note: Equality holds when z₁ and z₂ point in the same (or opposite) direction.

formulas.name: Argument
formulas.formula: tan α = |y/x|;  principal arg θ ∈ (−π, π]:  Q1 α,  Q2 π − α,  Q3 −(π − α),  Q4 −α;  arg(z₁z₂) = arg z₁ + arg z₂;  arg(z₁/z₂) = arg z₁ − arg z₂
formulas.mistake: Pick θ by quadrant — tan⁻¹(y/x) alone can be wrong.

formulas.name: Polar and Euler form
formulas.formula: z = r(cos θ + i sin θ) = re^{iθ};  z₁z₂ = r₁r₂ e^{i(θ₁ + θ₂)}

formulas.name: De Moivre's theorem
formulas.formula: (cos θ + i sin θ)ⁿ = cos nθ + i sin nθ

formulas.name: Square root of a + ib
formulas.when: Square root of a complex number.
formulas.note: If b is negative the imaginary part is negative.

formulas.name: Locus in Argand plane
formulas.formula: |z − z₀| = r: circle;  |z − z₁| = |z − z₂|: perpendicular bisector;  |z − z₁| + |z − z₂| = 2a (> |z₁ − z₂|): ellipse;  arg((z − z₁)/(z − z₂)) = constant: arc of a circle

formulas.name: Quadratic formula and discriminant
formulas.formula: x = (−b ± √D)/2a,  D = b² − 4ac;  D > 0 real distinct,  D = 0 real equal,  D < 0 complex conjugate pair;  D a perfect square (rational coefficients) ⇒ rational roots
formulas.note: With real coefficients, complex roots always come in conjugate pairs.

formulas.name: Sum and product of roots
formulas.formula: α + β = −b/a;  αβ = c/a;  α² + β² = (α + β)² − 2αβ;  |α − β| = √D/|a|

formulas.name: Equation from roots
formulas.when: Forming an equation from given roots.

formulas.name: Common root
formulas.formula: One common root of a₁x² + b₁x + c₁ = 0 and a₂x² + b₂x + c₂ = 0: (c₁a₂ − c₂a₁)² = (a₁b₂ − a₂b₁)(b₁c₂ − b₂c₁);  both roots common: a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂

formulas.name: Extreme value of a quadratic
formulas.formula: vertex of ax² + bx + c at x = −b/2a;  value = −D/4a;  a > 0 ⇒ minimum, a < 0 ⇒ maximum

examples.title: Modulus and argument
examples.problem: Modulus and principal argument of z = 1 + i√3?
examples.solution: |z| = √(1 + 3) = 2. In Q1, tan α = √3 ⇒ arg z = π/3. Polar: 2(cos π/3 + i sin π/3).

examples.title: Division
examples.solution: Multiply by the conjugate (1 + i): (1 + i)²/(1 + 1) = 2i/2 = i.

examples.title: Sum of squares of roots
examples.problem: α² + β² for the roots of x² − 5x + 6 = 0?

examples.title: Equal roots
examples.problem: For what k does x² + kx + 9 = 0 have equal roots?

examples.title: Minimum value
examples.solution: At the vertex x = 2 the value is 4 − 8 + 7 = 3 (= −D/4a = 12/4).

examples.title: Locus
examples.solution: z is equidistant from (1, 0) and (−1, 0) ⇒ perpendicular bisector x = 0, i.e. the imaginary axis.

topics.title: Argand plane
topics.explain: The x-axis is the real axis, the y-axis the imaginary axis. z = x + iy is the point (x, y). |z₁ − z₂| is the distance between two points. Multiplying by i rotates z by 90° anticlockwise.

topics.title: Rotation
topics.explain: z₂ − z₀ = (z₁ − z₀)(r₂/r₁)e^{iθ}: z₁ rotated about z₀ by θ. Equilateral triangle: z₁² + z₂² + z₃² = z₁z₂ + z₂z₃ + z₃z₁.

topics.title: Uses of ω
topics.explain: Roots of x³ = 1. Roots of x² + x + 1 = 0 are ω and ω². 1, ω, ω² are vertices of an equilateral triangle on the unit circle. Moduli of expressions like a + bω + cω².

topics.title: Nature of roots and the graph
topics.explain: y = ax² + bx + c is a parabola opening upward if a > 0. D > 0 ⇒ it cuts the x-axis twice; D = 0 ⇒ it touches; D < 0 ⇒ it doesn't cut (always positive when a > 0).

topics.title: Sign scheme and location of roots
topics.explain: Both roots greater than k: D ≥ 0, af(k) > 0, −b/2a > k. One root less than k and one greater: af(k) < 0. For a > 0, ax² + bx + c > 0 outside the roots.

topics.title: Symmetric functions
topics.explain: α³ + β³ = (α + β)³ − 3αβ(α + β). 1/α + 1/β = (α + β)/αβ. For an equation with transformed roots (like 1/α, α + 1), replace x by the inverse of that transformation.
